title: PGF curated privacy reference registry
purpose: Selected primary references and entry points; not a legal opinion, exhaustive legal inventory or compliance certification.
maintenance: Manual curation before each PGF release; see MAINTENANCE.md. Review-due dates do not schedule automated work.
scope: EU/EEA and Canada core; NIST/ENISA engineering references; limited UK/Swiss extensions and an explicit draft/proposal watchlist.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: General Data Protection Regulation — Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.status: in_force; check consolidated amendments and applicability
sources.curation_note: Core legal baseline. Use the version applicable to the processing date; an ELI link to the original act does not pin the latest consolidated text.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: Standard Contractual Clauses — Commission transfer resources (Decision (EU) 2021/914)
sources.status: 2021 transfer SCC resources; select the applicable module
sources.curation_note: Read the actual decision and clauses from this official page. SCC selection, recipient scope and supplementary measures are separate decisions.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: European Commission register of adequacy decisions
sources.status: living_register; scope and current validity must be checked
sources.curation_note: Check destination, sector, recipient eligibility and validity. An applicable Article 45 decision follows a different route from an Article 46 SCC/TIA assessment.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: Digital Operational Resilience Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
sources.status: in_force; applies from 17 January 2025 subject to entity scope
sources.curation_note: Financial-sector profile. Read applicable delegated/implementing rules; DORA and GDPR notification channels have different tests and clocks.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: EBA — Joint technical standards on major incident reporting
sources.curation_note: Entry point to reporting content, time limits and templates, including Delegated Regulation 2025/301. Check triggers, extensions and exceptions in the final legal text.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
sources.curation_note: Privacy interface only: roles, human oversight, notices and fundamental-rights assessment may overlap. The original act must be read with the 2026 AI Omnibus and applicable transition rules.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: European Commission — AI Omnibus enters into force
sources.curation_note: Official status explanation, not a substitute for the amending regulation. Distinguish Annex III and product-embedded high-risk rules and already applicable obligations.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: NIS2 Directive — Directive (EU) 2022/2555
sources.curation_note: Adjacent cybersecurity regime. Determine national implementation, entity scope and the sector-specific relationship with DORA before assigning obligations.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: German Stock Corporation Act — section 111
sources.curation_note: Separates management from supervision while permitting reserved consent matters. This is not a universal board model.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Guidelines 07/2020 on controller and processor concepts
sources.curation_note: Classify the role per activity before allocating obligations or selecting a contract. Guidance is not itself legislation.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Guidelines on Data Protection Officers — WP243 rev.01
sources.curation_note: Use actual tasks to assess independence and conflicts. Includes confidential access to the DPO, resources and DPIA advice.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: DPIA and high-risk processing — EDPB endorsement of WP248 rev.01
sources.curation_note: The nine criteria inform triage; a scoring questionnaire cannot override Article 35 or an applicable supervisory-authority list.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Guidelines 4/2019 — Article 25, data protection by design and by default
sources.curation_note: Connect design/default requirements to lifecycle decisions and evidence, rather than treating DPIA approval as the whole design process.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Recommendations 01/2020 — supplementary transfer measures
sources.curation_note: Mechanism-specific assessment of laws/practices and effective supplementary measures. Do not treat organisational risk acceptance as a cure for an ineffective transfer tool.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Guidelines 9/2022 — personal data breach notification under GDPR
sources.curation_note: Separate breach existence, recording, controller notification tests and processor-to-controller escalation. Includes controller awareness and phased reporting.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: Coordinated Enforcement Action 2023 — designation and position of DPOs
sources.curation_note: Findings and recommendations on resources, expertise, conflicts, independence and access to senior management; distinguish recommendations from statutory duties.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: CJEU — X-FAB Dresden, C-453/21
sources.curation_note: Case-by-case assessment of conflicting duties, including determining purposes and means. A RACI letter alone does not establish a conflict.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: CJEU — Data Protection Commissioner v Facebook Ireland and Schrems, C-311/18
sources.curation_note: Transfer safeguards and essentially equivalent protection. Read the judgment and its application to the selected mechanism.

sources.title: ENISA — Pseudonymisation techniques and best practices
sources.curation_note: Engineering techniques, adversaries and attacks. Pseudonymisation does not by itself establish anonymity.

sources.title: ENISA — Data Protection Engineering
sources.curation_note: Engineering reference for implementing protection principles; not a PGF certification scheme.

sources.title: NIST Privacy Framework — Version 1.0
sources.curation_note: Stable baseline for PGF function/category mapping. A conceptual crosswalk is not proof of compliance or effectiveness.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-226 — Guidelines for Evaluating Differential Privacy Guarantees
sources.curation_note: Check privacy unit, adjacency, accountant, composition and implementation hazards. Parameters and empirical attack scores are not legal safe harbours.

sources.title: NIST IR 8062 — Privacy engineering and risk management in federal systems
sources.curation_note: Reference vocabulary and privacy engineering objectives. Its federal-system context must be acknowledged when adapting it.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 — Security and Privacy Controls
sources.curation_note: Pin the control catalogue release when mapping PT and related controls. The landing page links CPRT; Rev.5 PDF and current catalogue updates are not interchangeable.

sources.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework — Version 2.0
sources.curation_note: Use for the InfoSec interface. Cybersecurity risk management does not replace privacy risk assessment.

sources.title: IIA — Global Internal Audit Standards, 2024
sources.curation_note: Reference independent assurance and board/audit-committee governance, including Standards6.2 and9.4. This is not a universal GDPR statutory requirement; do not reproduce the copyrighted standard.

sources.title: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA)
sources.curation_note: Determine commercial-activity, federal/provincial and cross-border applicability. GDPR lawful-basis tables do not transpose directly.

sources.title: Breach of Security Safeguards Regulations — SOR/2018-64
sources.curation_note: Read with PIPEDA sections10.1–10.3. Keep all required breach records; distinguish records from notification thresholds.

sources.title: Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector — P-39.1
sources.curation_note: Read the consolidated private-sector Act as amended by Law25. Do not import article numbers from the public-sector Act or assume PIPEDA and Quebec are identical.

sources.title: Regulation respecting the anonymization of personal information — A-2.1, r.0.1
sources.curation_note: Enabling laws include private-sector P-39.1 as well as the public-sector Act. Verify the current full text and its assessment/reassessment requirements before relying on clauses.

sources.title: OPC/OIPC — Getting Accountability Right with a Privacy Management Program
sources.curation_note: Direct programme-design reference for organisational commitment, programme controls and ongoing review. Guidance is distinct from legislation.

sources.title: OPC — Mandatory reporting of breaches of security safeguards
sources.curation_note: Operational explanation of real risk of significant harm, notification and records. Do not import the GDPR72h deadline.

sources.title: UK GDPR — official legislation portal
sources.curation_note: UK extension only. Read with DPA2018 and commenced DUAA2025 changes; EU and UK texts are distinct.

sources.title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025
sources.curation_note: Enactment is not the same as commencement of every provision. The portal response could not be rendered by the automated reader.

sources.title: Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection — SR235.1
sources.curation_note: Swiss extension only; the data protection adviser and consultation rules differ from the EU DPO model. Fedlex requires a JavaScript-capable reader.

sources.title: NIST Privacy Framework — Version1.1 development
sources.curation_note: Track separately from the final1.0 mapping. Do not combine draft and final control identifiers.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines02/2026 on Anonymisation
sources.curation_note: Relevant emerging guidance, explicitly not final. Recheck status before freezing a release.

sources.title: BillC-36 — Protecting Privacy and Consumer Data Act (45th Parliament, first session)
sources.curation_note: Track the actual legislative stage; it has not replaced PIPEDA. Direct tracker access was403; official indexed tracker and House Journals were checked.

sources.title: Digital Omnibus — Council negotiating position, 21October2026
sources.curation_note: Distinguish this data/GDPR/cyber proposal from the separate AI Omnibus. A proposed notification deadline is not the current GDPR deadline.

sources.group: EU and EEA — law and transfer mechanisms
sources.title: Data Privacy Framework List (U.S. Department of Commerce) — participating organisations
sources.jurisdiction: United States (EU–U.S. DPF, UK Extension, Swiss–U.S. DPF)
sources.status: dynamic_official_register; check the organisation record at the time of each transfer decision
sources.curation_note: Evidence source for the recipient's current participation, not a legal basis by itself. Record per flow: exact legal entity and covered entities, framework (EU–U.S. DPF / UK Extension / Swiss–U.S. DPF), HR or non-HR data, the official status wording, profile URL, checked_at, reviewer and evidence reference. The list is not copied into PGF; no vendor is endorsed. A special status such as 'Active – Re-certification under Review' is read with the official explanation, not converted to 'inactive'. The main page requires JavaScript.

sources.group: EU regulator guidance and case law
sources.title: EDPB — EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework FAQ for European businesses (16 July 2024)
sources.curation_note: Q3 explains how to check that a US recipient is certified and that the certification covers the data concerned (including HR data). Guidance, not law; the adequacy decision is the legal basis.

sources.title: Swiss–U.S. Data Privacy Framework — FDPIC announcement and DPF Swiss FAQ
sources.status: Swiss adequacy for certified US recipients applies from 15 September 2024 (FDPIC)
sources.curation_note: Separate Swiss legal route: it requires the recipient's Swiss–U.S. DPF certification and the Swiss legal basis; an EU–U.S. DPF certification does not by itself cover Swiss transfers. Companion FAQ: https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/program-articles/FAQs%20%E2%80%93%20Swiss%E2%80%93U.S.-Data-Privacy-Framework-%28Swiss%E2%80%93U.S.-DPF%29-%281%E2%80%934%29

sources.title: Canada Revenue Agency — Privacy Management Framework
sources.curation_note: Example of a compact departmental programme overview under the federal Privacy Act regime. Not a private-sector standard; no conformity with it or with the Privacy Act is claimed.

sources.title: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada — Privacy Management Framework
sources.curation_note: Second departmental example of a compact programme overview. Not a private-sector standard; no conformity is claimed.
